title: The Rise of the Supreme Court’s So-Called Shadow Docket

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在清晨4点半给总统打了电话，他接了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空探索了七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星的背后是什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 上千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60款超级圣代冰淇淋。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的队伍。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用一个不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 而且我喜欢用一口锅做完的菜，因为我讨厌洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》庆祝成立175周年，陪伴您理解世界，过好每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受nyt.com/subscribe上的特惠活动。

sentences.en: Hey there, it's Rachel.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是雷切尔。

sentences.en: I want to take a quick second to tell you about a fun little project that we're working on here at The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我想花一点时间跟大家聊聊我们在《每日新闻》制作的一个有趣的小项目。

sentences.en: It's something that we'll share later on as a bonus episode for New York Times subscribers.
sentences.zh: 这个内容我们稍后会作为《纽约时报》订户的专属番外节目推出。

sentences.en: And the idea is really simple.
sentences.zh: 这个想法其实很简单。

sentences.en: We want to talk to our fascinating, incredible colleagues here at The New York Times about who they are and how they do their jobs.
sentences.zh: 我们想和《纽约时报》那些迷人、优秀的同事聊聊他们是谁，以及他们是如何工作的。

sentences.en: And as part of that, we want to take questions from you, our listeners.
sentences.zh: 作为其中的一部分，我们想解答来自你们，也就是我们听众的问题。

sentences.en: We're going to start with games.
sentences.zh: 我们首先从游戏开始。

sentences.en: Wordle, connections, the crossword, the things so many of us do every single day.
sentences.zh: Wordle、Connections、填字游戏，这些我们许多人每天都在玩的游戏。

sentences.en: We're starting with the actual people who actually make those games.
sentences.zh: 我们将直接对话那些真正制作这些游戏的人。

sentences.en: So what are your questions?
sentences.zh: 那么，你们有什么问题呢？

sentences.en: Do you want to know what the Wordle editor thinks of your starting word?
sentences.zh: 你想知道Wordle的主编怎么看你用的第一个词吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to know how they come up with a new game?
sentences.zh: 你想知道他们是如何构思一个新游戏的吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to know if they ever cheat?
sentences.zh: 你想知道他们有没有作过弊吗？

sentences.en: Whatever your question is, you can send it to us by recording a voice memo and emailing it to dailysubscribers at nytimes.com.
sentences.zh: 不管你的问题是什么，都可以通过录制语音备忘录并发送电子邮件至dailysubscribers@nytimes.com来联系我们。

sentences.en: Okay, here's the show.
sentences.zh: 好的，节目开始了。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯，这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court has cleared the way for President Trump to remake American government, siding with the president over and over again.
sentences.zh: 最高法院为特朗普总统重塑美国政府铺平了道路，一次又一次地站在总统这边。

sentences.en: But many of these rulings lack something fundamental, an explanation for why the most important judges in the country came to their decision.
sentences.zh: 但其中许多裁决缺乏一个核心要素——解释为什么这个国家最重要的法官们会做出这样的决定。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Adam Liptak explains why the rise of the so-called shadow docket has sown confusion and, in some cases, frustration in courts around the country.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事亚当·利普塔克将解释为什么所谓的“影子 docket（应急审理日程）”的兴起，已经在全国各地的法院中引起了混乱，在某些情况下甚至是沮丧。

sentences.en: It's Monday, September 15.
sentences.zh: 今天是9月15日，星期一。

sentences.en: Adam, I think that when most people think of the Supreme Court, they imagine oral arguments and lawyers standing in front of justices making impassioned cases for their clients and
sentences.zh: 亚当，我想大多数人在想到最高法院时，脑海中浮现的都是口头辩论，律师们站在大法官面前，为他们的当事人慷慨陈词，

sentences.en: then the justices asking questions and writing these lengthy opinions and dissents.
sentences.zh: 然后大法官们提出问题，并撰写长篇大论的判决书和异议书。

sentences.en: But you recently wrote about how there's been this flurry of cases recently that are kind of the exact opposite of everything I just described, which felt a little bit surprising.
sentences.zh: 但你最近撰文指出，最近涌现出大量案件，它们几乎完全颠倒了我刚才所描述的一切，这让人感觉有点意外。

sentences.en: And I wondered if you could just start off by telling us what has been going on at the
sentences.zh: 我想知道你能否先给我们讲讲，最近

sentences.en: Supreme Court lately.
sentences.zh: 最高法院到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: So the Supreme Court is operating these days on two tracks.
sentences.zh: 所以，最高法院现在采取的是两条路线并行。

sentences.en: One of those tracks, the one you refer to, Rachel, is the merit stocket.
sentences.zh: 其中一条就是你提到的，雷切尔，正诉 docket（实体审理日程）。

sentences.en: On the merit stocket, people ask the Supreme Court to hear a case.
sentences.zh: 在实体审理上，人们请求最高法院审理案件。

sentences.en: If it does, it hears oral arguments.
sentences.zh: 如果法院同意，就会进行口头辩论。

sentences.en: The justices meet, vote, deliberate, exchange drafts.
sentences.zh: 大法官们会面、投票、审议并交换初稿。

sentences.en: And about 60 times a year, they issue long-involved, considered decisions, majority opinions, dissenting opinions, often 100 pages or more.
sentences.zh: 每年大约有60次，他们会发布长篇的、深入的、深思熟虑的判决，包括多数意见、异议意见，通常长达100页甚至更多。

sentences.en: And that's what we're used to.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们习以为常的形式。

sentences.en: Now, at the same time, on a separate track, there's the so-called, and people use different
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在另一条独立的轨道上，有所谓的——大家对这个有不同的

sentences.en: names for this, there's the shadow docket or the emergency docket, or lately some justices have been calling it the interim docket.
sentences.zh: 叫法，有人叫它“影子 docket”、应急审理日程，或者最近有些大法官称之为“临时 docket”。

sentences.en: But the short of it is, is that this happens really faSt.
sentences.zh: 但简而言之，这一切发生得非常快。

sentences.en: Parties race to the court.
sentences.zh: 各方争分夺秒地涌向法院。

sentences.en: They submit only very thin briefs.
sentences.zh: 他们只提交非常简短的简报。

sentences.en: There's no oral argument.
sentences.zh: 没有口头辩论。

sentences.en: And in a matter of weeks, the court issues orders deciding consequential matters in a way that will last a year or two in a very terse opinion.
sentences.zh: 在几周内，法院就会发布命令，以一种只维持一两年、非常简短的意见对重大事项做出裁决。

sentences.en: And this different procedure has really accelerated in the second Trump administration, which has
sentences.zh: 而在特朗普第二任期内，这种不同的程序大大加速了，

sentences.en: run to the court maybe 24 times already in its first seven or eight months in office.
sentences.zh: 在执掌白宫的前七八个月里，他们可能已经向法院去了24次。

sentences.en: That's a larger number than the Biden administration did over four years.
sentences.zh: 这个数字比拜登政府四年任期内的次数还要多。

sentences.en: It's a much larger number than the Obama and George W.
sentences.zh: 这比奥巴马和乔治·W·

sentences.en: Bush administrations combined.
sentences.zh: 布什两届政府加起来的数字还要大得多。

sentences.en: So order of magnitude, we're in a different area.
sentences.zh: 所以从数量级上来看，我们进入了一个完全不同的领域。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And also, the subject matter of these applications is really consequential.
sentences.zh: 而且，这些申请的主题也极其重要。

sentences.en: And the court has greenlighted immigration stops in L.A., canceling NIH grants, firing thousands of federal workers, discharging transgender service members.
sentences.zh: 法院为洛杉矶的移民执法开绿灯，取消国立卫生研究院（NIH）的资助，解雇数千名联邦雇员，开除跨性别现役军人。

sentences.en: It's essentially the entire Trump agenda.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是特朗普的全部议程。

sentences.en: OK, that helps me understand why something that I don't think I've really heard about before this week, suddenly it feels as though I'm hearing about it everywhere.
sentences.zh: 好的，这让我明白了为什么在这周之前我似乎从未听说过的事，现在突然感觉到处都能听到。

sentences.en: So can you just explain what is this?
sentences.zh: 所以你能解释一下这到底是什么吗？

sentences.en: How does it work?
sentences.zh: 它是如何运作的？

sentences.en: So here's how these cases typically arise.
sentences.zh: 这些案件通常是这样出现的。

sentences.en: A president, say President Trump, issues an executive order setting out some bold piece
sentences.zh: 一位总统，比方说特朗普总统，发布了一项行政令，提出了他的一些激进的

sentences.en: of his agenda, some program that gets challenged in court, and a federal district court judge says, I don't know yet.
sentences.zh: 政治议程，某个在法庭上面临挑战的项目，而联邦地区法院法官说，我目前还不知道。

sentences.en: I haven't had a chance to look at all the evidence.
sentences.zh: 我还没有机会查看所有的证据。

sentences.en: I don't know yet whether it's lawful or not.
sentences.zh: 我目前还不知道它是否合法。

sentences.en: But I'm going to maintain the status quo.
sentences.zh: 但我打算维持现状。

sentences.en: And the status quo is we didn't have this program yesterday.
sentences.zh: 而现状就是我们昨天没有这个项目。

sentences.en: Let's not have it today either.
sentences.zh: 今天也先不要有。

sentences.en: And I'm going to block this program for now while the case goes forward, because I think it might not be lawful.
sentences.zh: 在案件审理期间，我将暂时叫停这个项目，因为我认为它可能不合法。

sentences.en: The administration doesn't like that answer.
sentences.zh: 政府不喜欢这个答案。

sentences.en: And they'll go to an appeals court and say, would you pause this ruling?
sentences.zh: 于是他们会上诉到上诉法院说，你们能暂停这个裁决吗？

sentences.en: Because we think this ruling is wrong.
sentences.zh: 因为我们认为这个裁决是错误的。

sentences.en: The appeals court might well say, no, it's OK with us.
sentences.zh: 上诉法院很可能会说，不，我们觉得没问题。

sentences.en: Then within days, it goes to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 然后不出几天，案件就送到了最高法院。

sentences.en: And the Supreme Court is asked to pause that ruling blocking the initiative, not to rule on its ultimate lawfulness, just to say whether it can be in place or not.
sentences.zh: 最高法院被要求暂停那个阻止该倡议的裁决，而不是去裁决其最终是否合法，只是表态它是否可以付诸实施。

sentences.en: And the court does that very fast, generally without in-person deliberation among the justices, kind of shooting from the hip.
sentences.zh: 法院非常迅速地做到了这一点，通常是在大法官之间没有面对面审议的情况下，有点像是即兴做出决定。

sentences.en: And importantly, issues orders that contain either very little reasoning, a paragraph or two, or quite often, no reasoning at all.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，它发出的命令包含的理由非常少，只有一两个段落，或者很多时候，干脆没有任何理由。

sentences.en: It just says yay or nay, and you don't know why.
sentences.zh: 它只说行或不行，而你不知道为什么。

sentences.en: So it basically sounds like this is a process that allows decisions to both get expedited and also does not provide a lot of transparency into why they are made.
sentences.zh: 所以这听起来基本上是一个让决策得以加快，但同时又缺乏对决策原因透明度的过程。

sentences.en: Why has this procedure become more popular recently?
sentences.zh: 为什么这种程序最近变得越来越流行？

sentences.en: I mean, the basic answer is that presidents of both parties have been increasingly aggressive in trying to do stuff by executive order.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，最根本的回答是，两党总统都越来越激进地试图通过行政令来推行政策。

sentences.en: And that gives rise, kind of as night follows day, to court challenges, to court rulings,
sentences.zh: 这就像黑夜之后紧接着白昼一样，必然引发法庭诉讼、法院裁决、

sentences.en: to initiatives being blocked, and the Supreme Court being asked to weigh in on really short notice.
sentences.zh: 倡议被阻挠，以及最高法院被要求在极短时间内介入表态。

sentences.en: And I should say that this acceleration, this uptick, has exploded in the second Trump administration.
sentences.zh: 我得说，这种加速和激增在特朗普第二任期内呈爆发式增长。

sentences.en: And the administration thought that the Supreme Court will generally be sympathetic to them,
sentences.zh: 政府认为最高法院通常会同情他们，

sentences.en: either because it's a 6-3 Republican appointee majority that might be inclined to be sympathetic
sentences.zh: 原因要么是这是一个由6比3的共和党任命派占多数的法院，可能倾向于同情

sentences.en: to a Republican president or a court that in general defers to executive power of presidents of either party.
sentences.zh: 共和党总统，要么是该法院通常对两党总统的行政权力抱持尊重的态度。

sentences.en: But the Trump administration has gone to the Supreme Court over and over again in the knowledge that they are quite likely to succeed, and they have been.
sentences.zh: 但特朗普政府明知自己极有可能成功，还是一次又一次地求助于最高法院，而他们也确实如愿以偿了。

sentences.en: So what it sounds like is that the Trump administration has basically figured out that this is an effective
sentences.zh: 所以听起来，特朗普政府基本上已经弄清楚了，这是一种快速执行其议程的有效

sentences.en: strategy to execute their agenda quickly, and they have been proven right in the many decisions that we've seen handed down so far this year.
sentences.zh: 策略，而今年到目前为止我们看到的大量裁决也证明他们是对的。

sentences.en: But I feel like a lot of people listening might be thinking, like, wait a minute, don't the Supreme Court justices typically vote along party lines?
sentences.zh: 但我觉得许多听众可能会想，等一下，最高法院的大法官们通常不是按党派立场投票的吗？

sentences.en: There's a reason we call them conservatives or liberal justices, right?
sentences.zh: 我们称他们为保守派或自由派大法官是有原因的，对吧？

sentences.en: There is an element of politics in Supreme Court judging.
sentences.zh: 最高法院的审判中确实存在政治成分。

sentences.en: But in argued cases on the so-called merit stocket, they're unanimous like 40 percent of the time.
sentences.zh: 但在所谓实体审理的辩论案件中，他们有大约40%的情况下是全票通过的。

sentences.en: The number of cases that break strictly along the 6-3 line is like a large handful.
sentences.zh: 完全按照6比3的党派界限分裂的案件屈指可数。

sentences.en: And unusual alliances and weird permutations and strange bedfellows are not uncommon on the merit stocket.
sentences.zh: 在实体审理中，不同寻常的结盟、奇怪的排列组合以及意料之外的“同床异梦”并不少见。

sentences.en: So like in the normal course of business, you do see more agreement among the conservative and the liberal justices.
sentences.zh: 所以在日常业务中，你确实会看到保守派和自由派大法官之间有更多的共识。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But when we looked recently at just these emergency applications in the last two administrations, the picture is quite different.
sentences.zh: 但当我们最近只看过去两届政府的这些紧急申请时，情况就截然不同了。

sentences.en: There's a lot more partisan voting.
sentences.zh: 这里有更多的党派投票。

sentences.en: There are essentially no strange bedfellows.
sentences.zh: 基本上不存在什么意料之外的结盟。

sentences.en: The Biden administration did win a slight majority of its emergency applications.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府确实赢得了其紧急申请的微弱多数。

sentences.en: The Trump administration, far more successful, at 84 percent.
sentences.zh: 而特朗普政府则要成功得多，达到了84%。

sentences.en: But I don't think those are the most interesting numbers.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这些并不是最有趣的数字。

sentences.en: The most interesting numbers are when you look at the voting records of individual justices.
sentences.zh: 最有趣的数字是当你观察各个大法官的投票记录时。

sentences.en: And the right side of the court and the left side of the court are both completely playing to type.
sentences.zh: 法院的右翼和左翼完全是本色出演。

sentences.en: So Justice Alito may well be the most conservative member of the court, voted for President Trump 95 percent of the time.
sentences.zh: 因此，阿利托大法官很可能是法院中最保守的成员，在95%的情况下投票支持特朗普总统。

sentences.en: And President Biden, 18 percent of the time.
sentences.zh: 而支持拜登总统的比例只有18%。

sentences.en: That is a 77 percentage point gap.
sentences.zh: 这是一个高达77个百分点的差距。

sentences.en: I did that math because when you look at Justices Sotomayor and Ketanji Brown Jackson, probably the two most liberal members of the court,
sentences.zh: 我之所以算出这个数据，是因为当你看到索托马约尔和克坦吉·布朗·杰克逊大法官——这可能是法院中最自由派的两位成员时，

sentences.en: they also have a 77 percentage point gap, but going in the other direction.
sentences.zh: 他们也有77个百分点的差距，只不过方向完全相反。

sentences.en: Now, this is not completely apples to apples.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并不完全是同类比较。

sentences.en: They're not the same cases.
sentences.zh: 它们不是同一个案件。

sentences.en: They're different legal issues.
sentences.zh: 它们是不同的法律问题。

sentences.en: But in a sense, not.
sentences.zh: 但从某种意义上说，其实也是。

sentences.en: In a sense, it's the same fundamental legal issue.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这是同一个根本性的法律问题。

sentences.en: How much difference do you give the president?
sentences.zh: 你赋予总统多少权力？

sentences.en: And how do you calculate whether leaving a program in place causes harm to one side or the other?
sentences.zh: 你如何计算让一个项目继续存在是否会对某一方造成伤害？

sentences.en: That's the basic question in all of these emergency applications.
sentences.zh: 这是所有这些紧急申请中的基本问题。

sentences.en: And the justices I just mentioned come to very different conclusions, if not based on, at least correlated to, the president who they might be thought to like or dislike.
sentences.zh: 而我刚才提到的大法官们得出了截然不同的结论，这些结论至少与他们可能喜欢或讨厌的总统相关，甚至就是基于此。

sentences.en: Why do you think we see so much more partisanship in these emergency decisions?
sentences.zh: 你认为为什么我们在这些紧急裁决中看到了如此多的党派偏见？

sentences.en: I think the justices themselves will say they don't do their best work on short notice.
sentences.zh: 我想大法官们自己也会承认，他们在时间仓促时无法发挥出最佳水平。

sentences.en: That long consideration of briefs and arguments and deliberations helps them understand the issues, find consensus.
sentences.zh: 对简报、辩论和审议的长期考量有助于他们理解问题、寻找共识。

sentences.en: Find common ground.
sentences.zh: 寻找共同点。

sentences.en: Find common ground.
sentences.zh: 寻找共同点。

sentences.en: Find ways to rule maybe more narrowly, but with a greater majority.
sentences.zh: 寻找能够以更狭隘、但拥有更多数支持的方式做出裁决的途径。

sentences.en: When you're operating at this speed, things other than the law may take a greater role.
sentences.zh: 当你以这种速度运转时，法律之外的因素可能会发挥更大的作用。

sentences.en: Now, the justices will say, well, that's why we don't write anything, because we don't want to be locked in, because we haven't thought it through completely,
sentences.zh: 现在，大法官会说，这就是为什么我们不写任何东西的原因，因为我们不想被锁死，因为我们还没有完全想清楚，

sentences.en: because we're being required to give a quick answer.
sentences.zh: 因为我们被要求给出快速的回应。

sentences.en: And we will defer to another day the chance to give a more considered answer.
sentences.zh: 我们会把给出更深思熟虑答案的机会留到改天。

sentences.en: And they say that if you were to write something now, you'd be locked in, and it would be harder for you to come to a different conclusion later.
sentences.zh: 他们说，如果你现在写点什么，你就会被框死，以后要想得出不同的结论就会更加困难。

sentences.en: But the rise of this procedure, the rise of emergency orders, has real consequences for the work of the Supreme Court, and it's causing some real chaos in the legal system itself.
sentences.zh: 但这种程序的兴起、紧急命令的增多，对最高法院的工作产生了切实的后果，并且正在法律体系本身中造成真正的混乱。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写了Connections这个游戏，它是《纽约时报》游戏板块的拼图之一，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，我也喜欢试图捉弄你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是山姆·马祖斯基，我每天创作Spelling Bee和Letterboxd这两款游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚刚听到声音的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com/games开始今天的游戏。

sentences.en: Adam, I can imagine why these kinds of decisions might be sort of confusing, because these orders, as you explained, are issued really, really quickly.
sentences.zh: 亚当，我可以理解为什么这类决定可能会让人感到困惑，因为正如你所解释的那样，这些命令发布得非常非常快。

sentences.en: And the Supreme Court isn't explaining itself in great detail.
sentences.zh: 而且最高法院并没有详细解释自己。

sentences.en: So I wonder if you could give an example of a case that would allow us to see kind of how that lack of explanation leads to this confusion in real time.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望你能举出一个案件的例子，让我们看看缺乏解释是如何实时导致这种混乱的。

sentences.en: Well, just recently, there was a challenge to the immigration crackdown in the Los Angeles area, where, as you know, ICE agents were stopping detaining lots of people.
sentences.zh: 嗯，就在最近，洛杉矶地区出现了一起针对移民打击行动的诉讼，如你所知，当时移民及海关执法局的特工拦截并拘留了大量人员。

sentences.en: And Challenger said that violated the Fourth Amendment.
sentences.zh: 原告方提出，此举违反了美国宪法第四修正案。

sentences.en: They said it was indiscriminate racial profiling.
sentences.zh: 他们称这是无差别的种族 profiling。

sentences.en: And they persuaded a federal trial judge to issue an injunction that says, we're not saying you can't enforce the immigration laws,
sentences.zh: 他们说服了一名联邦初审法官下达了一道禁令，该禁令指出，我们并不是说你们不能执行移民法，

sentences.en: but saying you can't rely on certain factors alone or in combination.
sentences.zh: 而是说你们不能仅凭某些单一或组合的因素来采取行动。

sentences.en: And those factors were someone's apparent ethnicity.
sentences.zh: 而这些因素就是某人明显的外表族裔。

sentences.en: You can't stop somebody just for looking Hispanic.
sentences.zh: 你们不能仅仅因为某人看起来像西班牙裔就拦下他们。

sentences.en: Whether they speak Spanish or accented English, whether they're at a work site that you might associate with unauthorized immigrants, or the type of work people do, say,
sentences.zh: 不论他们说的是西班牙语还是带口音的英语，不论他们身处你们可能认为与非法移民有关的工作场所，还是他们从事的工作类型，比如，

sentences.en: landscaping or construction.
sentences.zh: 园艺或建筑。

sentences.en: And the Trump administration didn't like those restrictions.
sentences.zh: 特朗普政府对这些限制很不满。

sentences.en: They go to the appeals court, the Ninth Circuit.
sentences.zh: 他们上诉到了联邦上诉法院，即第九巡回上诉法院。

sentences.en: The Ninth Circuit won't pause it.
sentences.zh: 第九巡回法院拒绝暂停该禁令。

sentences.en: And they go to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 于是他们上诉到了最高法院。

sentences.en: And the Supreme Court rules for the administration in a decision that contains precisely zero reasoning.
sentences.zh: 最高法院做出了支持政府的裁决，而这份裁决包含的理由正好是零。

sentences.en: Like nothing.
sentences.zh: 就像什么都没有一样。

sentences.en: They didn't explain any part of the decision.
sentences.zh: 他们没有对裁决的任何部分作出解释。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We don't know whether it was because the parties challenging the order didn't have standing or whether the lower courts had ruled too broadly on immigration enforcement tactics.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道这是因为对该命令提出异议的当事方不具备诉讼主体资格，还是因为下级法院在移民执法策略上的裁决范围过宽。

sentences.en: The majority gave no reasons.
sentences.zh: 多数派没有给出任何理由。

sentences.en: All we know is the Supreme Court orders that, in Los Angeles at least, ICE agents are free to use these tactics to pick people up, at least for now.
sentences.zh: 我们只知道最高法院下令，至少在洛杉矶，移民及海关执法局特工可以自由使用这些策略来抓人，至少目前是这样。

sentences.en: Does it apply elsewhere?
sentences.zh: 这适用于其他地方吗？

sentences.en: We just don't know.
sentences.zh: 我们根本不知道。

sentences.en: So in other words, and I think this gets at the confusion that you were talking about earlier, if you are, for example,
sentences.zh: 所以换句话说，我认为这触及了你刚才所提到的混乱情况，如果你，比如说，

sentences.en: a judge in Chicago and you're dealing with this exact same type of issue, whether or not law enforcement can racially profile,
sentences.zh: 是芝加哥的一名法官，正在处理完全相同类型的问题，即执法部门是否可以进行种族 profiling，

sentences.en: you don't know how the Supreme Court made its decision.
sentences.zh: 你并不知道最高法院是如何做出这项决定的。

sentences.en: So therefore, you don't understand what the actual precedent is,
sentences.zh: 因此，你不明白真正的先例是什么，

sentences.en: and you are just basically guessing about whether or not your decision is an appropriate application of the Supreme Court's precedent.
sentences.zh: 你基本上只能去猜想你的裁决是否对最高法院先例的恰当适用。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，

sentences.en: one thing in this case in particular was that the trial judge's ruling looked at four factors and said that you can't alone or in combination relying on only those factors stop somebody.
sentences.zh: 这个案件的一个特别之处在于，初审法官的裁决审查了四个因素，并表示不能仅凭这些因素中的单一或组合来拦截某人。

sentences.en: Well, that raises a ton of questions, and the next judge may wonder, well, what about two or three of those factors, or what about apparent ethnicity by itself?
sentences.zh: 这引发了一大堆问题，下一位法官可能会想，那么其中两三个因素呢，或者仅仅是明显的外表族裔呢？

sentences.en: An ordinary merits decision would methodically work through these issues and give litigants and judges real guidance about what the law is.
sentences.zh: 一份正常的本案实质裁决会系统地处理这些问题，并为诉讼当事人和法官提供真正的指导，说明法律到底是什么。

sentences.en: Now, we haven't yet seen real-life examples of lower courts grappling with the quite recent decision on immigration stops in L.A., but in other cases involving federal grants
sentences.zh: 目前，我们还没有看到下级法院处理洛杉矶移民拦截案这一最新决定的现实案例，但在涉及联邦拨款的其他案件中，

sentences.en: and whether the president can fire the leaders of independent agencies, whether he can deport people to South Sudan, those cases have caused actual judges to be actually confused.
sentences.zh: 以及总统是否可以解雇独立机构负责人、是否可以把人驱逐到南苏丹，这些案件已经让真正的法官感到了真正的困惑。

sentences.en: Justice Neil Gorsuch, actually last month, in a case involving NIH grants,
sentences.zh: 就在上个月，大法官尼尔·戈萨奇在一起涉及国立卫生研究院拨款的案件中，

sentences.en: said that a federal judge in Boston had ignored the reasoning of a four-paragraph order in April in a different case.
sentences.zh: 指出波士顿的一名联邦法官在另一宗案件中忽视了4月份一份四段式命令的推理。

sentences.en: And that he should have understood that even though that wasn't a ruling on the merits, and whether, as Justice Gorsuch said, it was only probabilistic,
sentences.zh: 并且他本该明白，尽管那并非本案实质裁决，而且正如戈萨奇大法官所说，它仅仅具有概率性，

sentences.en: that it still had presidential force, and that judge had done something gravely wrong.
sentences.zh: 但它仍然具有总统效力，而那位法官犯下了严重的错误。

sentences.en: And that gave the judge, William Young of the federal district court in Boston, a real, I don't know what to call it, he actually went into a court hearing,
sentences.zh: 这让波士顿联邦地区法院的法官威廉·扬陷入了一种，我不知道该怎么称呼它，他实际上走进了一个法庭听证会，

sentences.en: and at length apologized, and said he didn't realize he had not meant to defy the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 进行了长篇大论的道歉，并表示他没有意识到自己并非有意违抗最高法院。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: That he was a Reagan appointee, he said in his 40-some years on the bench, he's never tried to defy a higher court ruling, he is committed to precedent.
sentences.zh: 他是由里根总统任命的，他在法官岗位上工作了四十多年，他说自己从未试图违抗上级法院的裁决，他一直致力于维护先例。

sentences.en: He's like, I'm not a troublemaker.
sentences.zh: 他好像在说，我可不是个惹麻烦的人。

sentences.en: He just didn't know.
sentences.zh: 他只是不知道而已。

sentences.en: And this is not an isolated incident.
sentences.zh: 这并不是个别现象。

sentences.en: Lots of judges are really struggling to figure out what kind of precedent a shadow docket ruling represents.
sentences.zh: 许多法官都在努力弄清楚影子 docket 裁决到底代表了什么样的先例。

sentences.en: The problem we have is the Supreme Court isn't giving us opinions, it's giving us signals.
sentences.zh: 我们面临的问题是，最高法院给我们的不是意见，而是信号。

sentences.en: Just last week, federal appeals court judges in Virginia debated this in open court.
sentences.zh: 就在上周，弗吉尼亚州的联邦上诉法院法官在公开法庭上就此展开了辩论。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court's action must mean something.
sentences.zh: 最高法院的行动必然有其含义。

sentences.en: It doesn't do these things just for the kicks of it, and we can't just blow past it.
sentences.zh: 它做这些事绝不是闹着玩的，我们也不能直接置之不理。

sentences.en: And you can hear them weighing how, on the one hand, these orders are quite opaque.
sentences.zh: 你可以听到他们在权衡，一方面，这些命令相当含糊。

sentences.en: But, I mean, I have to say, I kind of read the Supreme Court as telling us we are the ultimate deciders of the interim status of a case.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，我不得不说，我认为最高法院是在告诉我们，我们是案件临时状态的最终决定者。

sentences.en: How do we get around that here?
sentences.zh: 我们在这里该如何绕过这一点呢？

sentences.en: On the other hand, they have an obligation to follow Supreme Court precedent if they can figure out what that precedent is.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，如果他们能够弄清楚先例是什么，他们就有义务遵循最高法院的先例。

sentences.en: But they're telling us nothing.
sentences.zh: 但他们什么也没告诉我们。

sentences.en: And so you had one judge really bristling at the Supreme Court for putting them in this position, for giving them so little detail, so little guidance.
sentences.zh: 因此，有一位法官对最高法院将他们置于这种境地、提供如此之少的细节和指导感到非常愤怒。

sentences.en: We're out here flailing.
sentences.zh: 我们在外面苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: We're just in the water, thrown in the water.
sentences.zh: 我们就像被扔进水里一样，在水里扑腾。

sentences.en: Just give them some guidance.
sentences.zh: 哪怕给他们一些指导也好啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: No disagreement there.
sentences.zh: 这一点毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Adam, I think one of the previous recent times we've had you on the show was to discuss this growing tension between the lower courts and the Supreme Courts.
sentences.zh: 亚当，我想我们最近邀请你上节目的其中一次，是为了讨论下级法院与最高法院之间日益加剧的紧张关系。

sentences.en: And this feels like a really clear example of how that tension is playing out in the open.
sentences.zh: 这感觉就像是一个非常清晰的例子，说明这种紧张关系是如何公开上演的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in general, that is not the way the federal judicial system usually works.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，联邦司法系统通常不是这样运作的。

sentences.en: There's great respect and admiration across the levels of the judicial system.
sentences.zh: 司法系统的各个层级之间存在着极大的尊重和钦佩。

sentences.en: And people know their roles.
sentences.zh: 每个人都清楚自己的角色。

sentences.en: And this controversy, dispute, schism, and out in the open is really unusual.
sentences.zh: 而这种争议、争端、分裂以及公开化确实很不寻常。

sentences.en: I guess one thing I'm wondering is, it's clear why what you have outlined could be frustrating to a judge.
sentences.zh: 我想我感到好奇的一点是，你所概述的情况会让法官感到沮丧，这是显而易见的。

sentences.en: But why should an average person care that this is going on?
sentences.zh: 但为什么普通人要在乎这种事正在发生呢？

sentences.en: Well, if judges are confused, the people affected by these decisions are confused.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果法官感到困惑，那么受这些决定影响的人就会感到困惑。

sentences.en: And that's not a handful of people.
sentences.zh: 而且这可不是区区几个人。

sentences.en: Well, that's thousands, maybe tens of thousands of federal workers.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是成千上万，甚至可能是几万名联邦雇员。

sentences.en: It's many hundreds of thousands of immigrants.
sentences.zh: 那是几十万甚至上百万的移民。

sentences.en: These are decisions that are not abstractions.
sentences.zh: 这些都不是抽象的决定。

sentences.en: They are real-life, life-altering decisions from the court.
sentences.zh: 它们是来自法院的、现实生活中且会改变人生命运的决定。

sentences.en: Given all of the confusion this is causing for people and for the lower courts, I just want to ask, is this the only mechanism by which these cases can be decided?
sentences.zh: 鉴于这一切给人们和下级法院带来的困惑，我只想问，这是裁决这些案件的唯一机制吗？

sentences.en: Like, do they really have to be decided this quickly just because the government asks for them to be decided on this emergency basis?
sentences.zh: 比如说，难道真的必须以这么快的速度做出决定，仅仅是因为政府要求以这种紧急程序做出决定吗？

sentences.en: There is another way, and the court has done this occasionally.
sentences.zh: 还有另一种方法，法院偶尔也这样做过。

sentences.en: Instead of issuing an order based only on these thin stay application briefs, it could set the case down for argument.
sentences.zh: 不是仅仅根据这些单薄的暂缓执行申请简报来下达命令，而是可以安排案件进行辩论。

sentences.en: It could call for more briefs.
sentences.zh: 它可以要求提供更多简报。

sentences.en: It could do that pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 它完全可以很快做到这一点。

sentences.en: And maybe the answer is, in these hard cases, rather than moving at lightning speed,
sentences.zh: 也许答案是，在这些艰难的案件中，与其以闪电般的速度推进，

sentences.en: slow it down a little bit and give a more conclusive answer after briefing argument deliberation.
sentences.zh: 不如稍微放慢脚步，在听取简报、辩论和审议后给出一个更具决定性的答案。

sentences.en: The short answer is, no, it does not have to be this way.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答是，不，事情本不必如此。

sentences.en: There could actually be an in-between option.
sentences.zh: 实际上可以有一种折中方案。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But what's more common is that these same cases in which the court has temporarily green-lighted programs will come back to the court in due course, in a year, on the merits.
sentences.zh: 但更常见的情况是，法院暂时开绿灯的这些案件，最终会适时在一年内回到法院进行实质审理。

sentences.en: And they'll set it down for real arguments.
sentences.zh: 他们会安排真正的辩论。

sentences.en: And they won't necessarily go the same way.
sentences.zh: 而且结果不一定和之前一样。

sentences.en: In the Biden years, there were three instances where the court refused to lift injunctions blocking Biden programs, but ultimately ruled in favor of Biden.
sentences.zh: 在拜登执政期间，曾有三次法院拒绝解除阻止拜登计划的禁令，但最终作出了有利于拜登的裁决。

sentences.en: In the Trump scenario, it may be that when cases return to the court, Trump loses.
sentences.zh: 在特朗普的情况下，当案件回到法院时，特朗普可能会输。

sentences.en: But in the meantime, things will have happened.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，事情已经发生了。

sentences.en: If the court green-lights lifting immigration protections for hundreds of thousands of people, some of those people will have been deported.
sentences.zh: 如果法院为取消数十万人的移民保护开绿灯，其中一些人就已经被驱逐出境了。

sentences.en: If the court green-lights firing thousands of federal workers, maybe someday they'll go, you know what, you shouldn't have fired them.
sentences.zh: 如果法院为解雇数千名联邦雇员开绿灯，也许有一天他们会说，你知道吗，你们本来不该解雇他们。

sentences.en: But they got fired nonetheless.
sentences.zh: 但他们毕竟还是被解雇了。

sentences.en: They got deported nonetheless.
sentences.zh: 他们毕竟还是被驱逐出境了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So you can call these interim orders, provisional orders, temporary orders, but they have real-world immediate consequences that can't necessarily be undone.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以称这些为过渡性命令、临时命令、暂行命令，但它们具有现实世界中的即时后果，这些后果不一定能被撤销。

sentences.en: I wonder how you think we should understand the moment that the court is now in,
sentences.zh: 我想知道你认为我们应该如何看待法院目前所处的时刻，

sentences.en: in terms of whether what we are seeing represents a fundamentally different Supreme Court or a phase of the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 就我们所看到的究竟是一个根本上不同的最高法院，还是最高法院的一个阶段而言。

sentences.en: I think this could be a new normal with the court, which has for centuries operated in great deliberation.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能会成为法院的一种新常态，而法院几个世纪以来一直是以高度审慎的方式运作的。

sentences.en: There are scattered around the Supreme Court grounds little sculptures of tortoises,
sentences.zh: 最高法院的庭院周围散落着一些小海龟雕塑，

sentences.en: and that's a representation from the court that what they do is slow and deliberate and considered and not moving at lightning speed.
sentences.zh: 这代表着法院的作风是缓慢、审慎、深思熟虑的，而不是以闪电般的速度推进的。

sentences.en: But these days, seemingly half of the court's efforts are devoted to this kind of speedy, unexplained work.
sentences.zh: 但如今，似乎法院一半的工作都投入到了这种迅速且未经解释的工作中。

sentences.en: And remember that we have three branches of government.
sentences.zh: 请记住，我们有三个政府分支。

sentences.en: Two of them are elected.
sentences.zh: 其中两个是选举产生的。

sentences.en: They claim legitimacy by dint of having been elected by the public.
sentences.zh: 它们的合法性是通过公众选举产生的身份来获取的。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court, the justices, are obviously unelected.
sentences.zh: 最高法院的大法官显然是没有经过选举产生的。

sentences.en: And they claim legitimacy and authority by dint of reason,
sentences.zh: 他们是通过讲道理、

sentences.en: by dint of explaining themselves and persuading people that the issue before them has gotten their full attention and a careful opinion that you may not agree with.
sentences.zh: 通过自我解释并说服人们他们面前的问题已经得到了充分关注以及一份你或许不同意的缜密意见书来获取合法性和权威性的。

sentences.en: But at least you can follow it, at least you can engage with it, at least you can sort of test where it's right or wrong.
sentences.zh: 但至少你能跟上它，至少你能参与其中，至少你可以某种程度上检验它是对是错。

sentences.en: At a court that just says, like a parent would say to a child, why?
sentences.zh: 在一个对公众说——就像父母对孩子说的那样，“为什么？”

sentences.en: Because I said so.
sentences.zh: “因为我这么说的”——的法院面前，

sentences.en: That is a different version of the American justice system than the one we've been used to.
sentences.zh: 这与我们习惯的美国司法系统版本大不相同。

sentences.en: And it has the potential to reshape not only the Supreme Court, but American justice.
sentences.zh: 它有可能重塑的不仅是最高法院，还有美国的司法制度。

sentences.en: Adam, thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 亚当，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Rachel.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，雷切尔。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: Governor Spencer Cox of Utah provided new information about the background and political leanings of the 22-year-old accused of killing Charlie Kirk, saying that the suspect had,
sentences.zh: 犹他州州长斯潘塞·考克斯提供了关于涉嫌杀害查理·柯克的22岁嫌疑人的背景和政治倾向的新信息，称该嫌疑人，

sentences.en: quote, leftist ideology and that he had been in a romantic relationship with someone who is in the process of transitioning from male to female.
sentences.zh: 引用原话，具有“左翼意识形态”，并且他曾与一个正在经历从男到女变性过程的人谈恋爱。

sentences.en: I will say that that person has been very cooperative with authorities.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，那个人一直非常配合当局。

sentences.en: What we have learned specifically is that this person did not have any knowledge, was shocked when they found out about it.
sentences.zh: 我们具体了解到的是，这个人完全不知情，在发现此事时感到震惊。

sentences.en: Cox said on NBC's Meet the Press that the romantic partner, who lived with the suspect, had provided investigators with private messages that incriminated the alleged gunman.
sentences.zh: 考克斯在全国广播公司（NBC）的《会见新闻界》节目中表示，与嫌疑人同居的恋爱伴侣向调查人员提供了 incriminating（含罪证的）私人信息，指证了这名所谓的枪手。

sentences.en: Cox also said that the suspect appeared to have been, quote, radicalized sometime after dropping out of college,
sentences.zh: 考克斯还表示，嫌疑人似乎在大学辍学后的某个时候被“激进化”了，

sentences.en: and that the man had spent much of his time immersed in online gaming, message boards, and part of what Cox called the, quote, deep, dark Internet.
sentences.zh: 这名男子将大量时间沉浸在网络游戏、留言板以及考克斯所谓的“深暗网络”的一部分中。

sentences.en: And in a live stream from the set of Kirk's podcast, his wife Erica spoke for the first time publicly since the assassination, vowing that her husband's work would continue.
sentences.zh: 在柯克播客节目的现场直播中，他的妻子埃里卡自暗杀事件发生以来首次公开讲话，发誓她丈夫的事业将会继续下去。

sentences.en: If you thought that my husband's mission was powerful before, you have no idea.
sentences.zh: 如果你以前认为我丈夫的使命很强大，那你根本一无所知。

sentences.en: You have no idea what you just have unleashed across this entire country and this world.
sentences.zh: 你根本不知道你们刚刚在这个国家和全世界引发了什么。

sentences.en: You have no idea.
sentences.zh: 你根本不知道。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Mary Wilson, Ricky Nowitzki, and Michael Simon-Johnson.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由玛丽·威尔逊、里基·诺维茨基和迈克尔·西蒙-约翰逊制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Rob Zipko, Lexi Dio, and Devin Taylor, and was engineered by Alyssa Moxley.
sentences.zh: 由罗布·齐普科、莱克斯·迪奥和德文·泰勒剪辑，艾莉莎·莫克斯利担任音频工程。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是本期《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Rachel AbraMs.
sentences.zh: 我是雷切尔·亚布拉姆斯。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台受到严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了许多自称是改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就一直陷入一场残酷、混乱有时又惊心动魄的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都市》节目中，我和主持人莎拉·科尼格将带你了解那些试图维持影响力却最终失去控制的人的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。

sentences.en: So, let's see.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我想想。

sentences.en: I love you.
sentences.zh: 我爱你。

sentences.en: Let's see.
sentences.zh: 让我想想。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
